subject: Launch ingress profile and SLA bump request - PixelBay pilot
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T08:15:00-08:00
Subject: PixelBay pilot: expected ingress profile + request for temporary SLA bump

Ava / Lauren —

Quick summary: PixelBay (images-to-caption startup) is going live with a user acquisition campaign next week and asked for a short runway of higher request throughput for their pilot. They want us to guarantee a lower tail latency for 48 hours and raise per-minute rate limits for their account during the promo window.

Projected traffic (from PixelBay marketing):
- Day 1 (soft launch): 75k requests over 6 hours (peak 600 r/s)
- Day 2 (promo pulse): 320k requests over 12 hours (peak 1,800 r/s)
- Most requests are short text-only prompts (avg tokens: 40 in, 20 out) with image attachments handled client-side.

Ask: Can infra provide a temporary rate-limit increase + SLO exception for 48 hours for PB account and advise on required work to avoid cascading throttles across shared pools? Attaching their ingress profile and a draft mutual ops plan (MOP).

Attachments: pixelbay_ingress_profile_v2.xlsx, pixelbay_mop_draft.pdf

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PixelBay pilot: expected ingress profile + request for temporary SLA bump

Thanks Rafa — forwarding to infra and ops for feasibility. Couple of immediate questions for sizing and risk:
1) Can we confirm the percent of requests that will hit the LLM generation route vs embeddings/rerank? (helps with batching expectations)
2) Do they require streaming responses? That affects tail-latency planning.
3) Are they ok with a prefetched KV-cache key for repeated image prompts?

Lauren — I left the MOP draft in the attachments. Would product sign off on a temporary model fallback set (smaller quantized variant) if we need to absorb peak?

Neha / Marcus — can you run a quick sim with their peak profile and return: estimated p95/p99 latencies per model, and whether a rate-limited isolation pool or account-level burst bucket is the safer approach?

--
Ava Chen
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PixelBay pilot: expected ingress profile + request for temporary SLA bump

Folks —

Ran a quick local sim against the ingress_profile_v2 numbers Rafael shared. Assumptions: payload sizes small, avg seq len 60, model = redwood-open-4b. Results (approx):
- Peak 1,800 r/s into shared pool -> expected p95 ~ 220 ms, p99 ~ 640 ms with current batching; p99.9 spikes > 1400 ms under cold-kv conditions.
- If we route PixelBay to a dedicated burst pool (replicated 2x with autoscaling cap) during the 48h window, we can keep p99 < 700 ms reliably. Cost trade: ~2.5x infra minutes for duration.

Options to reduce risk/cost:
- Temporary model fallback to quantized redwood-4b-q for non-critical endpoints (saves ~35% GPU time)
- Enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts (they indicated many repeated caption templates)
- Throttled burst bucket: allow sustained baseline at 600 r/s, permit token-bucket bursts up to 2,000 r/s for 10s windows with refill tuned to expected average.

If product ok with fallback and legal signs off on an SLA note, ops can spin the burst pool. Need approval by EOD to meet PixelBay timeline.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
SRE Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PixelBay pilot: expected ingress profile + request for temporary SLA bump

Thanks — product perspective below:

- Fallback model: Approved for non-critical caption-generation endpoints. We will provide a smaller checkpoint (redwood-4b-q) behind a feature flag and mark it in the MOP so PixelBay understands subtle score differences.
- Streaming: PixelBay does not require streaming; single response OK. That simplifies tail latency.
- API-level controls: We'll add a temporary per-account policy to gate heavy evaluation endpoints (no more than 5 parallel requests per API key for the heavy route).

Action items:
- Product to ship the feature flag & model alias by 11/29 18:00 PST.
- Security/legal to include a one-paragraph SLA addendum (48h exception) in the MOP. Rafael, can you confirm PixelBay is OK with the addendum language?

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Product Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PixelBay pilot: expected ingress profile + request for temporary SLA bump

Lauren — confirmed with Sara at PixelBay. They accept the fallback model and the one-paragraph SLA addendum. They also asked for a short technical runbook in case we need to throttle or failover.

Sara's note (copied from an earlier thread):
> We can tolerate small differences in captions during the campaign — our priority is lower latency for promotional users. We'll share telemetry if you want to tune prefetching.

Rafa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PixelBay pilot: expected ingress profile + request for temporary SLA bump

All — ops has greenlit the plan. Summary of decisions and next steps:

- We will provision a 2x replicated burst pool for PixelBay from 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-12-03T00:00:00Z with autoscaling caps tuned to their peak.
- Product will enable model alias + feature flag (redwood-4b-q fallback) by 2026-11-29 18:00 PST per Lauren.
- Security will append the 48h SLA addendum to the MOP; Rafael please get PixelBay sign-off on the doc.
- Ops will enable account-level burst token-bucket policy and a kill-switch route to fallback pool (runbook stub in the MOP).
- Cost: estimated additional infra spend ~ $18k for the 48h window; finance approval not required for this pilot but flagged for review.

I'll open a short incident-style Slack channel and pin the MOP and runbook. Marcus

Marcus Lin
Head of Ops | Redwood Inference
